title: The Mona Lisa
subject: art
description: Painted by **Leonardo da Vinci** between **1503** and **1519**, *The Mona Lisa* has become the absolute icon of the Louvre. Technique, mysterious smile… and a flight in **1911** that changed everything.

hero.hook: A smile, a theft, a myth: how a portrait became the most famous work in the world.

blocks.text: *The Mona Lisa*, painted between **1503** and **1519** by **Leonardo da Vinci**, is the most visited painting in the world. Exhibited at the **Louvre**, it fascinates as much by its technique as by its history. It's not just a beautiful portrait. It is a myth made by art, science and a news item.
Why this face rather than another? Because Leonardo concentrated innovations there, and because a spectacular flight made it famous on a global scale.

The portrait begins in Florence around **1503**. The sponsor is the merchant **Francesco del Giocondo**. The model would be his wife, . But Leonard never delivers the painting. He kept it, retouched it for years, and took it to France, where he died in **1519**. [[Lisa Gherardini]]

blocks.caption: The Mona Lisa at the Louvre: a small poplar panel that has become a global icon.

blocks.text: His signature technique is : glazes, very thin layers, which erase the contours. No more hard line. The face melts in the air. Leonardo also adds the : the distant landscape turns blue and softens, as in the real vision. [[Leonardian sfumato]] [[Atmospheric Perspective]]

sections.title: The smile that plays with the eye

blocks.text: The famous smile is not just a painted emotion. He plays with our . When we stare at the model's eyes, the edges of the retina see the mouth in soft shadows: the smile seems present. When you look directly at the mouth, it diminishes. [[Peripheral vision]]

blocks.caption: The more you stare at it, the more the smile seems to disappear.

blocks.text: Leonardo, both a painter and a scholar, studied optics. The mystery of the smile rests in part on a precise knowledge of how the human eye processes shadows.
Result: the face seems alive, changing, almost conscious of our gaze.

In the 19th century, *The Mona Lisa* was admired, but not yet the number one work in the Louvre. Everything changed on **August 21, 1911**. , an Italian glazier from the museum, steals it: it's . He hides it under his blouse and goes out quietly. [[Vincenzo Peruggia]] [[flight of the Mona Lisa (1911)]]

blocks.caption: 1911: the absence of the painting makes the headlines and creates a star.

blocks.text: The investigation turns into a scandal. The poet  is imprisoned for a time.  is questioned. When the painting reappears in **1913**, it is no longer just a painting. He's a celebrity. [[Guillaume Apollinaire]] [[Pablo Picasso]]

Today, painted on poplar wood, it lives behind a , in an air-conditioned display window. Acid attacks, throwing objects: protection has become necessary. And the parodies, from Duchamp to the Internet, prove that it has become a universal language. [[Bulletproof glass]]
